member.name: P:Havit.Blazor.GoogleTagManager.HxGoogleTagManagerOptions.EnableInitialPageViewTracking
member.summary:
Whether is pushed for the page the document was loaded with. Default is true.
The GTM snippet already announces a document load on its own (the container's built-in Page View trigger, plus a pageview event pushed for backwards compatibility), so with the default the first page of a session is announced twice - once as pageview and once as . That is what you want when the container treats as the single source of truth and ignores pageview.
Set to false when the container instead uses pageview (or its built-in Page View trigger) for real document loads and only for the navigations that follow. Without it those containers count the landing page of every session twice.
Only automatic tracking is affected - an explicit call always pushes.

member.name: T:Havit.Blazor.GoogleTagManager.HxGoogleTagManagerPageViewTracker
member.summary:
Initializes Google Tag Manager and tracks page-views to the GTM data-layer.
The component covers all render modes:
Static SSR and prerendering: the GTM snippet is emitted inline as a <script> tag directly into the HTML response (see the .razor file), so GTM starts loading while the page is still being parsed. No JS interop is available in this phase.
Static SSR with enhanced navigation: the inline snippet is not executed again when Blazor patches a new page into the DOM, so page-views for enhanced navigations are pushed by the Havit.Blazor.GoogleTagManager.lib.module.js JS initializer, which listens for the enhancedload event.
Interactive rendering (Server, WebAssembly, Auto): page-views are pushed in reaction to , which is what covers navigations handled by the interactive router. When the page was prerendered, GTM is already initialized by the inline snippet; otherwise the first push initializes it through JS interop.
Initialization and automatic page-views are deduplicated in JavaScript through shared window.hxGoogleTagManager state, so more than one instance of the component (for example one in App.razor for the earliest possible GTM load and one in the layout to cover interactive routing) is safe and does not produce duplicate events.
Full documentation and demos: https://havit.blazor.eu/components/HxGoogleTagManager

member.name: M:Havit.Blazor.GoogleTagManager.HxGoogleTagManagerPageViewTracker.GetInitializationScript
member.summary: Returns the inline GTM snippet for static SSR/prerendering. It intentionally repeats what HxGoogleTagManager.js initialize() does - the snippet has to run during HTML parsing, long before any ES module can be imported - and joins the same window.hxGoogleTagManager state, so whichever of the two runs first is the one that initializes GTM.
